Alert Rule

A specific, configurable criterion or threshold in monitoring tools that, when met or exceeded, triggers an automated alert.

Questions and answers

Questions and answers

What is Alert Rule?

In this glossary, Alert Rule refers to: A specific, configurable criterion or threshold in monitoring tools that, when met or exceeded, triggers an automated alert.

How is Alert Rule used in IT and DevOps?

In IT and DevOps communication, this term appears in contexts such as: "An alert rule triggers a notification if the system's memory usage exceeds 85% for more than five minutes."

Why does Alert Rule matter in IT and DevOps?

Alert Rule matters because it supports clear communication in Observability contexts for DevOps Engineers, SREs, and Platform Engineers. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as AWS Certification, Azure Certification, ITIL v4, and CKA/CKAD.

Who uses Alert Rule?

Alert Rule is mainly used by DevOps Engineers, SREs, and Platform Engineers.

Definition

A specific, configurable criterion or threshold in monitoring tools that, when met or exceeded, triggers an automated alert.
